# Akut Kirurgi Databasen

**Akut Kirurgi Databasen** (AKDB) is the central national clinical quality database for emergency surgery in Denmark, dedicated to monitoring and improving the care, diagnostics, and treatment of high-risk acute abdominal surgical patients [^src17]. Operating under the [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]] (RKKP), the database's annual reports are published and administered by the [[sundhedsvaesenets-kvalitetsinstitut|Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut]] [^src21], [^src35]. The database's steering group is chaired by [[peter-svenningsen|Peter Svenningsen]] [^src1].

### Purpose and Clinical Indicators
The primary significance of AKDB lies in its comprehensive tracking of clinical quality through a series of standardized process and outcome indicators. These include [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] (antibiotic treatment within 3 hours), [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] (CT scanning within 120 minutes), [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] (preoperative optimization), and time-to-surgery metrics like [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] and its supplementary variants [[indikator-4x|Indikator 4x]] and [[indikator-4y|Indikator 4y]] [^src2], [^src6], [^src24]. Postoperative care is monitored via early mobilization ([[indikator-6|Indikator 6]]), nutrition ([[indikator-7|Indikator 7]]), and epidural use, while patient outcomes are rigorously evaluated using 30-day and 90-day mortality rates ([[indikator-9|Indikator 9]], [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]], and [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]]), often stratified by comorbidity indices such as the [[charlson-score-0|Charlson Score]] and [[asa-score|ASA score]] [^src2], [^src13], [^src30]. 

### Data Infrastructure and Methodology
AKDB's data infrastructure relies primarily on routine registrations in the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]] (LPR), marking a shift toward standardized national data collection [^src1], [^src17]. To construct its population and indicators, the database integrates data from the [[cpr-registeret|CPR-registeret]], the [[den-nationale-labdatabank-dnl|Den Nationale Labdatabank]] (DNL), the [[dansk-anaestesi-database-dad|Dansk Anæstesi Database]] (DAD), and the [[sygehusmedicinregisteret|Sygehusmedicinregisteret]] (SMR) [^src17], [^src35]. The database's methodology follows guidance from the [[sundhedsdatastyrelsens-teknikergruppe|Sundhedsdatastyrelsens teknikergruppe]] and excludes specific departments (like gynecology and urology) via the [[sundhedsvaesenets-organisationsregister-sor|Sundhedsvæsenets Organisationsregister]] (SOR) [^src17]. Local validation against the [[epj|EPJ]] (Electronic Patient Record) is mandated to ensure data accuracy and correct population capture [^src36].

### Historical Context and Evolution
The database evolved from earlier registries, notably succeeding the [[danish-clinical-register-of-emergency-surgery|Danish Clinical Register of Emergency Surgery]], and its clinical indicators are heavily informed by evidence from the [[pulp-trial|PULP trial]] and the national quality improvement initiative [[lkt-akut-kirurgi|LKT Akutkirurgi]] [^src18], [^src29]. Over time, the database has adapted its metrics; for instance, in 2018, the steering group ([[styregruppen|Styregruppen]]) decided to cease monitoring bleeding ulcers, and in 2022, new codes for preoperative optimization were approved for analysis [^src4], [^src18]. Recent reports cover the periods from September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023 (published in February 2024), and September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024 (published in February 2025) [^src1], [^src20]. Regional bodies, including [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]], actively provide feedback on the database's indicators, highlighting ongoing challenges with data registration and clinical alignment in systems like NordEPJ [^src19], [^src38].

- 2018: Styregruppen besluttede, at 2023 ville være det sidste år med monitorering af blødenede ulcera (akut-kirurgi-databasen)
